correctness.rationale: Two equal-length multisets have a common three-symbol output exactly when the sum of their coordinatewise minima is at least three. Correcting exactly n−3 deletions and correcting up to that number are equivalent here, since any common longer output contains a common three-symbol submultiset. Disjoint heavy-coordinate sets bound the number of heavy codewords by four. Light words have sum at most eight, and any two light words have overlap at least 2n−8. At n=5 coexistence forces their coordinatewise maxima to be all twos, hence their two coordinates of multiplicity two must be complementary; no third light word can satisfy both compatibility constraints. The four pure vectors plus the listed light additions attain all the resulting upper bounds. In particular the stated n=9 threshold is sharp.
residual_risks: The finite replay is corroboration; the heavy/light argument proves the infinite range.
No ordered-word channel or classification of all optimal codes is claimed.

value.rationale: The three-survivor transition is a natural problem and the theorem is mathematically useful as a reference. As a separate present finding, however, it gives no invariant, improved bound, or new structural conclusion beyond the existing exact quaternary catalogue statement. The short light-vector argument and finite replay re-establish the same known exact fact; this is not an independently distinct valuable remainder under the exact-invariant standard.
residual_risks: This is not a negative assessment of the usefulness of the underlying theorem, and does not decide who established it first.
